title: Streamline build-init and adopt sparse dependency mounts
creator: Liam Ortiz
description:
Summary:
We are seeing significant CI flakiness and long wall-clock times caused by full dependency re-installs and repeated toolchain setup across many jobs. This ticket introduces a two-part modernization: (1) standardize the build-init step into a lightweight, deterministic shim that installs only what changed, and (2) adopt a sparse-dependency mount strategy (via BuildKit/kaniko-style mounts + a read-through cache bucket) so jobs reuse cached layers and avoid reinstalling unchanged packages.

Motivation / Problem Statement:
- Median CI job time for backend/unit tests has regressed ~2x over last year due to dependency churn and repeated install steps.
- Docker layer churn (frequent ADD/COPY/apt steps) invalidates build cache; changing unrelated files causes full rebuilds.
- Toolchain upgrades are brittle because installs are performed inline in job containers rather than a controlled prebuilt toolchain image.
- Current caching approach is brittle: long TTLs, large artifact blobs, and low local reuse for PRs.

Goals / Acceptance Criteria:
- Cut median CI backend build/test job runtime by >= 35% (measured across 2 weeks of PRs).
- Achieve a dependency cache hit rate >= 80% for non-major-version changes.
- Reduce cache upload size by 40% via sparse mounts (only changed deps transferred).
- No increase in CI flakiness (flake rate must not rise beyond baseline +1%).
- Rollout must support immediate rollback to current pipeline if issues observed.

Design / Approach:
1) Build-init shim
   - Introduce a small build-init script (packages/redwood-ci/build-init.sh) used by all pipeline templates. The shim will:
     * Read a normalized deps manifest (yarn.lock / package-lock.json / go.sum / pyproject.lock) to compute a deps fingerprint.
     * Mount a per-repo per-fingerprint cache directory (via BuildKit cache exporter/import or NFS bucket) and run a sparse-install that only fetches missing packages.
     * Install toolchain components (node, pnpm, Go toolchain) from pinned prebuilt toolchain images when possible.
   - The shim is intentionally minimal: no network fetches unless cache miss.

2) Sparse dependency mounts and cache layout
   - Use BuildKit frontend features to mount a repository-level deps cache as a shared layer. For language runtimes that don't support this, use a small sidecar container that provides a read-through cache via HTTP (cache-proxy).
   - Cache layout: /cache/{repo}/{lock-fingerprint}/{lang}/{version}/ where each entry is stored as individual package blobs rather than monolithic tarballs to minimize upload size on partial changes.
   - Implement a transparent TTL policy and automatic compaction job (retention: keep last 90 days or last 200 fingerprints).

3) Prebuilt toolchain images and pinning
   - Publish base toolchain images tagged with semantic toolchain versions and git-stamped metadata (labels). Pipelines should reference digest pins for determinism.
   - Introduce a lightweight image stamp process to cut a new toolchain image after validated upgrades and publish release notes.

4) CI templates and orchestration changes
   - Update central pipeline templates to call build-init.sh as the first step. Replace ad-hoc install steps in 20 highest-frequency repositories in initial rollout.
   - Add conditional fallback: if import of cache fails, fallback to current install path and report metric.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary, 1 week): Integrate build-init into core infra repo and 3 low-risk repos (infra-infra, infra-ci, docs). Measure cache hit rates and build times.
- Phase 2 (gradual, 2 weeks): Expand to 20 highest-frequency repos (backend services and SDKs). Turn on sparse mounts for languages with known support.
- Phase 3 (full, 2 weeks): Default pipelines across org use build-init; remove redundant inline install steps and deprecate per-repo toolchain scripts.
- Each phase includes a rollback gate: if median job time does not improve or flake rate rises >1%, revert to previous pipeline template and run a postmortem.

Testing & Validation:
- Unit tests for build-init shim behavior (fingerprint calculation, cache lookup semantics).
- Integration test harness in ephemeral runner that simulates: full fresh build, minor deps change, and major version bump.
- Load test the cache-proxy with synthetic requests to validate read latencies and concurrent clients.

Metrics / Dashboards to add:
- Build time histogram (median + p95) pre/post rollout.
- Cache hit rate by repo and language.
- Cache upload size delta per job.
- Flake/failed-job rate.
- Toolchain image usage and pin drift (how many jobs still using digest vs tag).

Links / Artifacts:
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ci-cache-sparse-mounts (draft)
- Prototype PR (build-init + cache-proxy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/12345
- Benchmark notebook: Google Drive /team/infra/ci-cache/benchmark-2026-02-10.ipynb

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Some package managers (legacy pip setups) don't support per-package blob layout — mitigation: fall back to compressed archive cache for these languages and prioritize Go/Node first.
- Risk: Cache poisoning (corrupted cache) — mitigation: verify blob checksums and use fingerprinting; if corruption detected, invalidate and rebuild.
- Risk: Increased complexity for on-prem/private deployments — mitigation: provide an optional NFS-backed mode and document setup in private deployment runbooks.

Acceptance & Done Criteria:
- All high-frequency repos use build-init in stable pipelines.
- Dashboards show target improvements for 14 consecutive days.
- Migration playbook and rollback steps are documented in Confluence and added as README in infra repo.
